title: Controlling CSS with code
objective: Change how things look from JavaScript with style, classList, CSS variables and data-* attributes
story: Your ship now moves and keeps time; now it's time for looks! Today you'll **control CSS** with JavaScript and build themes, effects and color pickers.

sections.title: element.style: properties one by one
sections.body:
Every element has a `style` object. Dashed CSS names are written in **camelCase** here (`background-color` → `backgroundColor`), and values are text, so don't forget the unit:

```js
const box = document.querySelector("#box");
box.style.backgroundColor = "#f7df1e";
box.style.width = "150px"; // not 150, but "150px"
```

`box.style` only shows what was written directly on the element. To see the final value that comes from the CSS rules, use `getComputedStyle(box).width`.

sections.title: States with classList
sections.body:
Instead of writing lots of styles one by one, write the look as a **class** in CSS and only add or remove the class in JavaScript:

```
.shield.active { border-color: #26c6da; background: #e0f7fa; }
```

```js
shield.classList.add("active");      // add
shield.classList.remove("active");   // remove
shield.classList.toggle("active");   // remove if it's there, add if not
shield.classList.contains("active"); // true / false
btn.classList.toggle("active", color === "#f7df1e"); // add if the condition is true, remove if not
```

sections.title: CSS variables
data-* attributes
sections.body:
Attributes starting with `data-` in HTML are a way to add your own information to an element. In JavaScript they're read and written with `dataset`:

```js
// <button data-color="#e53935">Crimson</button>
btn.dataset.color;                    // "#e53935"
document.body.dataset.mode = "night"; // <body data-mode="night">
```

CSS can select by these attributes too: `body[data-mode="night"] #panel { ... }`. That way, when one value changes, the whole look changes.

tasks.title: Planet color
tasks.prompt:
The planet's color comes from the CSS variable `--planet`. When any button with a `data-color` attribute is clicked:

- set the color to the button's `dataset.color` with `document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--planet", ...)`,
- write the variable's new value into `#current` like `Color: #1e88e5` (read it with `getComputedStyle(...).getPropertyValue("--planet")` and `trim()` it).

challenge.title: Panel mode
challenge.prompt:
Write the `setMode(mode)` function:

- it sets `document.body.dataset.mode` to `mode` (the CSS changes the panel's color based on it),
- it adds the `selected` class to the button whose `data-mode` equals `mode` and removes it from the others,
- it writes `Mode: night` into `#mode-label`.

When any `[data-mode]` button is clicked, it calls `setMode` with its own mode. When the page opens, `setMode("day")` runs.
challenge.html: Control panel

project_task.title: Theme and effects
project_task.prompt:
Let's add color and effects to the game. The ship's color comes from the CSS variable `--ship-color`.

- `setShipColor(color)`: sets `--ship-color` to `color` (`document.documentElement.style.setProperty`).
- When any `[data-color]` button inside `#colors` is clicked, it calls `setShipColor` with its own `dataset.color`.
- `flashHit()`: when the ship is hit, the play field (`#field`) flashes red: it adds the `hit` class and removes it **150 ms later** (`setTimeout`).
